question: The Prime Minister laid the foundation stone for the National Referral Centre for Wildlife in which city in 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Junagadh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **2025**, the **Prime Minister of India** laid the **foundation stone** for the **National Referral Centre for Wildlife** in **Junagadh, Gujarat**.
 
• The centre is being established to strengthen **wildlife health management**, **advanced veterinary care**, and **disease diagnosis** for wild animals.
 
• It will function as a **specialised national-level facility** to handle complex wildlife cases and provide expert support to wildlife veterinarians across the country.
 
• The facility is strategically located near the **Gir landscape**, which is the only natural habitat of the **Asiatic Lion (Panthera leo persica)**.
 
• The centre will contribute to strengthening India’s **wildlife conservation infrastructure**, research, and capacity building in **wildlife medicine**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct option is 2.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gir National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary**

 
 
• Located in **Gujarat**, near **Junagadh** and **Gir Somnath districts**.
 
• It is the **only natural habitat of the Asiatic Lion** in the world.
 
• Established as a **wildlife sanctuary in 1965**.
 
 
 
• **Asiatic Lion**
 
 
• Scientific name: **Panthera leo persica**.
 
• Conservation status: **Endangered** on the **IUCN Red List**.
 
• India’s Asiatic lion population is mainly concentrated in the **Gir landscape of Gujarat**.
 
 
 
• **Wildlife Conservation in India**
 
 
• Governed under the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**.
 
• India has more than **100 national parks** and over **500 wildlife sanctuaries**.
 
• Major conservation initiatives include **Project Tiger (1973)**, **Project Elephant (1992)**, and the **Asiatic Lion Conservation Project**.
 
 
 
• **About Junagadh**
 
 
• A historic city in **Gujarat,** located at the foothills of the **Girnar Hills**.
 
• Known for important sites such as **Girnar Temple**, **Uparkot Fort**, and proximity to **Gir National Park**.
